reference_items.stem:
This table shows temperatures at various times on four days.

| TEMPERATURE | | | | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| | 6 a.m. | 9 a.m. | Noon | 3 p.m. | 6 p.m. |
| Monday | 15° | 17° | 24° | 21° | 16° |
| Tuesday | 20° | 16° | 15° | 10° | 9° |
| Wednesday | 8° | 14° | 16° | 19° | 15° |
| Thursday | 8° | 11° | 19° | 26° | 20° |

[Image: Thermometer]

On which day and at what time was the temperature shown in the table the same as that shown on the thermometer?
reference_items.figure_description: A vertical thermometer labeled "Thermometer" at the bottom. The scale on the right has labeled marks at 5°, 10°, 15°, 20°, 25°, 30°, 35°, and 40°, with individual 1-degree tick marks between them. The shaded column of liquid inside the thermometer reaches exactly 24° (one tick mark below 25°).

PQRSTU is a regular hexagon. What is the measure of the angle QUS?

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A beaker of water which has reached boiling point is allowed to cool. The temperature of the water is recorded at five minute intervals, and a temperature-time graph is drawn.

Cooling Curve

[Image: Graph of cooling curve]

About how many minutes did it take for the water to cool the first 20 degrees?
reference_items.figure_description: A line graph titled "Cooling Curve" on a grid. The vertical axis is labeled "Temperature (°C)" with grid lines and numerical labels from 20 to 100 in increments of 20 (20, 40, 60, 80, 100), with 0 at the origin. The horizontal axis is labeled "Time (minutes)" with grid lines and numerical labels from 0 to 50 in increments of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50). A smooth curve starts at (0, 100) and decreases monotonically toward the right, passing through approximately (5, 74), (10, 55), (15, 43), (20, 37), (25, 32), (30, 28), (35, 24), (40, 22), (45, 21), and ending at (50, 20).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Which angle in the figure has a measure closest to 45°?

[Image: Circle divided into angles p, q, r, and s]
reference_items.figure_description: A circle contains a vertical diameter dividing it into left and right halves. From the center, two additional line segments (radii) are drawn: one extending to the left edge at roughly 9 o'clock (slightly below horizontal), and another extending down and to the right at approximately a 45-degree angle from the vertical. Four central angles are labeled: angle q is in the upper-left quadrant (between the upward vertical radius and the left radius, roughly 90°); angle p is in the lower-left quadrant (between the left radius and the downward vertical radius, roughly 90°); angle r is in the upper-right (between the upward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, an obtuse angle of roughly 135°); and angle s is in the lower-right (between the downward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, roughly 45°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
The diagram shows a system for locating points

[Image: A group of 6 concentric circles with origin “O”. Degrees from 0 to 360 are marked in 10 degree intervals where 0 and 360 are marked on a line “A” that goes across all circles. The 6 concentric circles are labeled from 1 to 6 along line “A”.]

In this system, the position of a point P is described by its distance from origin, O, and the amount of counterclockwise turn from a baseline OA to OP. Thus, the coordinates of P are (5, 340°).

A. Mark the points B (3, 30°) and C (4, 120°) on the graph above.
B. Draw the angle BOC. What is the measure of angle BOC?

Angle BOC = ____°

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

Choose the value closest to it.
